claim: A counterexample should be typed before repair: global-only (hidden assumption in the proof), local-only (a proof step is wrong but the claim survives), or both (add the failing lemma as an explicit condition). Each type calls for a different repair, and Pease turned this into a runnable decision procedure.
schema_part: O refute, repair-by-type sub-routine
agent_test: Give the agent a proof as explicit numbered steps. On a counterexample, force it to test each step and emit a type label, then pick repair by type. Compare with a free-form fix-it prompt at equal tokens on seeded flawed proofs and claims.
note: Gap search: no study tests typing with an LLM. Error type (local mechanical vs other) does predict where a diagnostic helps (d07).

claim: Informal proofs must be split into separately testable steps for local-versus-global typing to work. Separately, fault location in reasoning traces is the hard part, so explicit steps are a precondition for repair.
schema_part: S proof or plan state with explicit steps
agent_test: Compare error localisation and repair on traces with and without enforced step structure at equal tokens.

claim: In Pease's HRL tests the best response to a refuted conjecture was plain surrender (modification limit 0). Allowing up to 3 modifications modified everything, even uninteresting claims. Only some claims (animal taxonomy) were worth saving. Self-scored, no baseline.
schema_part: G budget on rescue versus drop / O refute
agent_test: Add a worth-saving gate (interestingness, plausibility) before any repair. Compare with always-repair and always-drop at equal tokens.
note: Gap search: thesis confirms the 42-session design (10 phases x 20 steps) and that the outcome is the students own interestingness (circular). Independent LLM evidence d06 and d08 shows restart beating repair at larger budgets, which supports surrender-then-restart, but not Pease limit 0 itself.

claim: Overspecialising a claim (adding exceptions and lemmas until it covers little) is a named failure, 'baby with the bath water'. The thesis proposes tracking how specialised a conjecture has become but never tested this.
schema_part: G repair budget / memory (claim scope)
agent_test: Log claim scope (share of original cases still covered) after each repair. Reject repairs below a threshold. Compare final usefulness against unconstrained repair.

claim: Exception-barring can be automated and checked by a model finder. Theorem Modifier gave a valid modification for 83% of 98 invented non-theorems (average 3.1 each) and 7 of 9 (78%) real TPTP non-theorems.
schema_part: O refute/repair
agent_test: Validate each exception-bar proposal with a cheap executable checker. One lab only (Colton and Pease). The three lines disagree on HR steps (300 vs 3000).
note: Gap search: HR steps for Theorem Modifier are 3000 (thesis ch. 12, with Otter and MACE at 10 s); 300 is not in the thesis. 83% of 98 and 7 of 9 confirmed against the thesis text. No modern replication found.

claim: Monster-barring (redefining terms to exclude the counterexample) can yield useful definitions (group-axiom-like). It is also the main way an agent silently changes the question. In LLM proof agents this shows up as altering the problem statement to make it easier.
schema_part: G statement fidelity / S fixed claim text
agent_test: Compare the final answer's statement word by word against the original. Count silent restatements with and without the check.

claim: Without an external check, model self-correction does not help reasoning and can hurt. Verified in the paper: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8 over two rounds; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 then 89.0. Earlier gains came from oracle labels.
schema_part: G no unverified self-judgement as evidence
agent_test: Compare a critique-and-revise round with no tool against a single answer and against resampling at equal tokens.

claim: Locating the fault is the bottleneck of self-repair, not fixing it. With the true wrong step given, backtracking fixes traces (tracking shuffled objects +23.53 on wrong traces, -11.11 on right ones). The best model finds the mistake only 52.87 overall (GPT-4, direct step prompting).
schema_part: O refute: locate first, then repair
agent_test: Two-stage refute: locate the step with an executable or independent check, then repair. Compare with one-shot reflect at equal tokens.
note: Gap search: ProcessBench and FaithSieve give reading-only localisation numbers; see K25.

claim: Executable or tool feedback gives repair gains that model-only feedback does not. CRITIC without tool 42.0/67.3/34.9 vs with tool 50.0/72.7/38.7. Self-Debug MBPP GPT-4 72.8 to 80.4 with unit tests vs +3.6 without execution. Reflexion HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1.
schema_part: G execution beats opinion / O test
agent_test: At equal tokens compare repair loops fed by code execution against loops fed by model critique, on counterexample-style tasks.

claim: Repair is not free. At equal sample budget it is about break-even with fresh sampling (GPT-4 on APPS: 10 drafts plus 1 repair each 1.05x of pass@20; 2 drafts plus 10 repairs 0.97x). Better feedback (human 52.60 vs GPT-4 33.30 repair success) is what lifts it.
schema_part: G equal-token control / budget allocation
agent_test: Always run a best-of-N resampling control at the same token count when judging any refute-repair loop.
note: Gap search: in Lean, repair is clearly worse than fresh sampling at equal tokens, not break-even; see K24.

claim: A self-written check can pass wrong answers and stop the loop at a false pass. Reflexion MBPP Python false-positive rate 16.3% vs 1.4% on HumanEval, and it lost to the baseline there (77.1 vs 80.1 in the paper table).
schema_part: G a check counts only if independent / S verdict state
agent_test: Seed wrong candidates that pass the agent's own tests. Measure how often the loop stops early with and without independently written tests.

claim: Propose-test-refine of rules works only with a symbolic interpreter. ACRE 64.0 direct to 82.5 (T=3, N=5); self-refine with the LM as interpreter only 70.0. No gain on List Functions (65.1 to 62.4); MiniARC fell (33.1 to 18.7). Models tend to patch the single failing example instead of rethinking the rule.
schema_part: O refute / G executable interpreter
agent_test: Same rule-induction task, interpreter = code vs LM, equal tokens. Count patch-only edits.

claim: Generating many explicit hypotheses, then testing them as code, beats direct prompting on ARC (GPT-4, 100 tasks): 17 direct, 23 program only, 30 LLM-summarised hypotheses, 33 human-selected, 45 human-written.
schema_part: O generate hypotheses plus execute-check
agent_test: ARC-style items: hypothesis list plus executed test vs direct program, equal tokens. Partial support from the Qiu family of results.

claim: Models that can solve a problem often cannot falsify a wrong solution. REFUTE: best RandSearch success 8.3% (o3-mini high) while solving up to 44-48.7%. With the correct solution given, success rises only to 15.1% (DeepSeek-V3) and 9.9% (R1). On average 35% of RandSearch samples end in an invalid counterexample.
schema_part: O refute: adversarial test generation needs search
agent_test: Give the agent code execution and a brute-force-compare scaffold for refuting candidates. Measure find rate against plain prompting at equal tokens.
note: Gap search: REFUTE has only incorrect solutions, so false refutation cannot be measured on it.

claim: University-level counterexample use is weak in open models and strong only in frontier reasoning models. COUNTERMATH F1: open 7B about 30, Qwen2.5-Math-72B 41.8, GPT-4o 59.0, o1-preview 60.1, R1 80.7 per text. SFT on 1,025 samples gave only +2.8 F1 (38.3 to 41.1).
schema_part: none (model capability)
agent_test: Not a scaffold test. Use as a difficulty sanity check.

claim: Training only on counterexample output teaches the output shape and breaks truth recognition (Qwen3-4B true-theorem recognition 0.27 to 0.00 after SFT). Counterexample Pass@1 on n=201: base 0.30, SFT 0.35, RLVR 0.50 (paired delta +0.199 [0.13, 0.27]). Prompt-only analogue: a refute-biased prompt that calls true claims false.
schema_part: G calibration: also test true claims
agent_test: Include true claims in every refute test set. Report the false-refutation rate beside the find rate.

claim: Dropping a hypothesis from a proved theorem is a cheap, verifiable source of false conjectures with known counterexamples (exception-barring in reverse). Two groups built corpora: 575K Lean problems from 212,463 seeds; 4,707 SymCE items with a 97.7% accurate verifier.
schema_part: O refute test bed (evaluation, not agent part)
agent_test: Build a small mutation test set to evaluate the agent's refute operator.

claim: Generate-then-filter by code is low-yield and failures are mostly syntactic. Of 757 outputs, 420 unique; 109 (25.95%) refuted by GAP code, 40 (9.52%) not refuted; 271 (64.52%) code did not run. Survivor share by model: GPT-4o 26.60%, Gemini 4.64%, Claude 4.49%.
schema_part: O generate plus execute-filter
agent_test: Count executable-check failures separately from real refutations. Fix the harness before judging idea quality.

claim: Counterexample-driven refinement of a real conjecture benefited from a counterexample search kept separate from the pattern learner. In the knot signature work, ML found patterns, and humans with a new dataset of about 36,000 knots found counterexamples and revised the bound.
schema_part: O refute / memory (counterexample store)
agent_test: Keep a persistent counterexample store and rerun every revised conjecture against it.
note: Gap search: AutoGraphForge shows the store dynamics but no LLM and no no-store arm.

claim: Real mathematical talk is counterexample-heavy. 34% of MathOverflow responses gave examples or counterexamples and 37% contained corrected errors. In mini-polymath 33% of 174 comments were examples or counterexamples. A misleading name (windmill) created a misconception.
schema_part: S naming / G name drift
agent_test: Descriptive only. Use as a prior on operator frequency and for a definitions glossary in memory.

claim: Proof-generated definition is only one way to justify a definition. Werndl adds three more from one case study (ergodic theory). Concept revision should allow more than one justification route.
schema_part: O concept-revision
agent_test: Qualitative. Offer the agent a justification menu when revising a definition and check consistency.

claim: No study found runs a Lakatos-labelled LLM loop (monster-barring, lemma-incorporation, concept refinement) with a matched resampling control. LLM work measures pieces only. Pease's own evaluation had no baseline.
schema_part: whole schema (the main test to run)
agent_test: Run Lakatos-typed repair vs untyped reflect vs best-of-N at equal tokens on seeded false claims.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Lemma-level iteration with executable verification can certify progress on an open problem. Gilbert-Pollak Steiner ratio lower bound 0.824 to 0.8559; with bottleneck reflection removed, no improvement over 10 rounds.
schema_part: O lemma-incorporation (links to lemma discovery)
agent_test: Hard to replicate cheaply. Test the idea: reflection on the binding bottleneck vs random lemma proposals.

claim: At equal tokens, repairing a failed formal proof from its error message did not beat a fresh restart. Lean, MiniF2F: sequential pass@64 repair 44.5% vs restart 62.8% (Qwen) and 24.5% vs 75.3% (DeepSeek-Prover 7B); at 200k tokens repair trails by 25.9 and 73.5 points. Repair prompts carry about 80 times the input tokens. A separate prover family shows self-correction ahead at small budgets (57 vs 48 on PutnamBench at pass@32) and restarts ahead at large ones (93 at pass@2048 vs 86).
schema_part: G equal-token control / surrender then restart
agent_test: Run repair for at most 2-3 rounds, then restart fresh; compare with pure restart at equal total tokens including input tokens.
note: Two preprints, different groups. The second is a system-to-system comparison and confounded by training. Formal Lean setting where the verifier gives a clean diagnostic.

claim: Finding the first wrong step by reading only is much weaker than with formal evidence, and extra reading samples do not close the gap. FaithSieve (Qwen3.5-9B, BIG-Bench Mistake subset, 200): formal-evidence pipeline 61.0 exact; direct 51.0; majority of 241 samples 51.0; reviewer panel at equal tokens 52.0; challenge-and-defence reading agent at 124% tokens 55.5. The formal pipeline used about 152 times the tokens of one direct judgement. ProcessBench: GPT-4o F1 51.4 on OlympiadBench vs o1-mini 87.2.
schema_part: O refute: locate by executing where possible
agent_test: On seeded flawed proofs, compare executor-based location, independent re-derivation of each step, and challenge-and-defence reading at equal tokens.
note: Preprint evidence from one group for the 152x cost; reasoning-mode models read far better than chat models.

claim: Repair loops silently change the claim, and meaning drift is not rare, but no seeded-set rate for LLM proof repair exists. An Isabelle audit found 16 of 100 original declarations changed, including a theorem weakened to assume three of four requirements. Statute formalisation repair left 15-45% NLI meaning drift. A protected-statement diff check rejected a trivially weakened theorem that the prover accepted.
schema_part: G statement-fidelity check around every repair
agent_test: Seed claims with known statements, run repair loops, and count statement changes with and without a diff-of-claim check; confirm repair success is not lowered.
note: Three independent sources agree drift exists; none gives a rate over a seeded proof-repair set.

claim: A claim shown to the model as someone else's work is corrected far more often than the same claim in its own turn. Adoption of a planted wrong claim was about 83% from own thought vs at most 3.3% from an external role; correction rose 23 to 93 points when relabelled. Self-distrust prompts did not help (0-23.3%).
schema_part: O refute: present the draft as third-party
agent_test: Run the refute pass in a fresh context with the draft labelled as an outside submission; compare with same-context reflect at equal tokens.
note: Preprint, 30 tasks per cell, planted errors. An external label also raises wrong-claim acceptance if it says ground truth.

claim: The monster-barring threshold in Pease's thesis is not one constant. Single-agent runs: up to 30-40% good. Multi-agent runs: 0-10% good, 10% hypothesised best. Mixed runs: best when students averaged 40-50%. The coded default is 15%. The earlier contradictions in the evidence lines are three different experiments, not an error. Number theory 97% is a degenerate score where no monster was proposed.
schema_part: none (do not carry numbers)
agent_test: Not to be transferred; any threshold must be set by an outcome measure on our own tasks.
note: Self-scored against the author's expected monsters; three toy domains.

claim: The only measured surrender signals are cheap counts on stored cases. In Pease's 42 sessions the best were: interestingness relative to the theory average, zero modifications, and plausibility = (supporting - counterexamples)/supporting at threshold 0.7. Domain-of-application (scope left) was not useful. The outcome measure was the agents' own interestingness, so these are hypotheses for us, not findings.
schema_part: G budget on rescue versus drop (signal candidates)
agent_test: Log plausibility and relative value before each repair; check offline which predicts repair success better than the repair-round count.
note: Circular outcome; inconclusive on threshold values per the thesis.

claim: Hidden-lemma discovery in Pease's system uses two surprise tests built on construction ancestry: (1) an entity is the only counterexample to a strengthened claim P->Q&R, found by walking Q's ancestors; (2) the claim holds only vacuously for an entity (antecedent false). Demonstrated on the cylinder example only; no LLM version or comparison with 'what did the proof assume?' exists.
schema_part: O refute: hidden-lemma probe
agent_test: Prompt A: find the odd-one-out case that breaks a strengthened version; prompt B: check each step for a vacuous antecedent; prompt C: what did the proof assume. Compare on seeded proofs with a known hidden lemma at equal tokens.
note: One worked example in the thesis.

claim: REFUTE cannot measure false refutations (all items are incorrect solutions). COUNTERMATH can: it has True/False statements (about 88% True by the pie chart) scored by macro F1, so a prompt-only agent's false-refutation behaviour can be read from recall on True items. Combine REFUTE (find real counterexamples) with correct-solution negatives or COUNTERMATH True items.
schema_part: test bed for the refute operator
agent_test: Report per-class recall on True and False items plus find-rate on REFUTE, all at equal tokens.
note: The 88% share is read from a garbled figure; no direct false-refutation rate in the paper.

claim: A persistent store of counterexamples pays mostly in the first round and shows a fixed point. AutoGraphForge: 494-793 new witnesses in round 1 (20-28% growth of a 2,860-graph store), 39-164 in round 2, 3-21 in round 3; four of five partitions stopped at round 5, one at round 9. Separate shards missed 1,413 refutations at merge (a shared store matters). No arm without the store, no LLM.
schema_part: memory: counterexample store
agent_test: Run the LLM with and without a store of past counterexamples and count rounds wasted on rederived refutations at equal tokens.
note: Graph theory with cheap evaluation; no LLM loop.

claim: Repair helps where the error is local and mechanical. With a correct diagnostic the gain was +34.0 points on Lean-3-syntax predecessors and +26.5 on unknown-identifier errors, but only +4.3 and +4.0 elsewhere. Even then repair (29 solved) trailed plain retry (35).
schema_part: O refute: decide repair or restart by error type
agent_test: Classify the failure as local-mechanical or structural; repair the first, restart the second; compare with always-repair and always-restart.

claim: The 2017 Lakatos dialogue game with argumentation semantics (Pease, Lawrence, Budzynska, Corneli, Reed, Artificial Intelligence 246) has an implemented worked example but no quantitative evaluation or baseline in its record. Whether multi-agent challenge and response helps is unmeasured.
schema_part: none (design idea only)
agent_test: If used, keep claims, counterexamples and objections as a labelled graph; test against a plain list.
note: Only the publisher record and abstract were read; PDF blocked.
